english.title: Breach safeguards in relation to examination of material - bulk equipment interference warrant
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) deliberately selected for examination material, namely **(..SPECIFY MATERIAL..) ,obtained under a bulk equipment interference warrant, in breach of a requirement imposed by section 193 or 194 of the Investigatory Powers Act, 2016, namely **(..SPECIFY REQUIREMENT..), knowing or believing that the selection of that material did not comply with that requirement
english.legislation: Contrary to section 196(1) of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
selected for examination any material obtained under a bulk equipment interference warrant
knowing or believing that the selection did not comply with a requirement imposed by section 193 or 194 of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016
deliberately selected that material in breach of that requirement

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
INDICTMENT: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.Note:
In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force (01/12/20), the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.
